judged_text: The literal string "refresh_token" is written into the parsed credential data whenever it lacks refresh_token — which the minimum schema guarantees in sharing mode by stripping the field — and callers persist that placeholder into credential.key with nothing marking it as a sentinel. A self-hoster who enables sharing (Office365's real refresh_token is overwritten by this sentinel on the first sync refresh) and later removes CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has every affected credential send the literal string "refresh_token" to the provider as its actual refresh token, killing those integrations with an invalid_grant that gives no hint the stored value is a placeholder.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly writes a literal placeholder when `refresh_token` is absent: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), it validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not require `refresh_token`, so the placeholder path is expected. Office365 then merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and persists it via `prisma.credential.update(...)` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), overwriting the real refresh token with the sentinel. If the self-hoster later removes `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, subsequent refreshes will use the stored literal "refresh_token" as the actual refresh token, breaking the integration as described.
